story: At 9:17 on this humid Saturday night at Rosa's house in Sumter Oaks, the neighbors have gathered in her kitchen and dining room, where Gary is content and keeping the cart parked until the board signs off. Donna is carrying in the peach cobbler and setting it out beside the ice cream, while Hal offers to haul the cornbread and table wherever Rosa points. Rosa, feeling cheerful and grateful, tells Donna the cobbler is the reason she isn't getting up from the table, and that this is exactly the neighborhood she hoped the Loop would be.
events: Donna (rosa kitchen): Carry the peach cobbler in and set it out with the ice cream

gary.thought_process: Hal just offered to help carry things and told me the cart staying parked was the right call. The ice is already in the kitchen from last tick, so I should answer him and put him to work on something real rather than let the offer hang. Rosa and Donna just walked in too, and Saturday at Rosa's table with the cobbler is exactly what I've been looking forward to. The cart stays in the garage until the review board signs off, so there's no need to fuss about that tonight. Best move is to thank Hal, point him at the kitchen where Rosa can use the help, and keep the evening moving.

parameters.content: Evening, Hal, and thanks. Cart's staying put till the board signs off, no sense risking a notice. The ice is already in the kitchen, so check with Rosa on what else she needs hauled to the table.

donna.thought_process: We're all at Rosa's now and it's past 9 PM. Rosa said the table's set and my cobbler needs to go to the kitchen. I should do that first rather than keep chatting. After that I can work on getting Gary locked in for the next pickleball session.

parameters.content: Carry the peach cobbler in and set it out with the ice cream

hal.thought_process: It's Rosa's dinner and everybody's here: Gary, Donna, Rosa. The old complaints are settled and I've been keeping the peace, so the notebook can stay in my pocket tonight. Gary's already been put to work hauling ice. I've got my own job, the cornbread and the table, so I'll find out from Rosa where she wants them rather than stand around. A sergeant doesn't leave supplies sitting on the porch.

parameters.content: Evening, Rosa. Cornbread's in hand and I'll carry the table wherever you want it. Just point and I'll have it squared away.

rosa.thought_process: Everyone I wanted is finally under my roof: Gary, Donna, and Hal, all in my house. It's 9:17 PM, so dinner has clearly happened or is winding down, and my goal of getting all three at one table has been met. I shouldn't repeat invitations. The natural move is to be a good host, say something warm, and thank them for each bringing a dish and pitching in. Quiet hours start at 10, so a gentle note about winding down and tomorrow's pickleball is natural. I'll address Donna and keep it short.

parameters.content: Donna, that cobbler is the reason I'm not getting up from this table. Thank you for pulling everyone together tonight, this is exactly the neighborhood I hoped the Loop would be.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
